notation.meaning: Projection (hat) matrix: turns $\mathbf{y}$ into fitted values

blocks.md: Most directions get both stretched and turned when a matrix acts on them, but a few special directions only get stretched. Those are the eigenvectors, and the amount of stretch along each is its eigenvalue. Together they summarise what a matrix does: their sum is the trace, their product is the determinant, a zero eigenvalue means the matrix cannot be inverted, and their sizes tell you whether a dynamic system settles down or explodes.

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.md: They show up whenever you need to know whether a matrix is invertible, positive definite or stable.
$\mathbf{v}$ is a direction that $A$ only stretches (by $\lambda$), never rotates.
$A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v} \iff (A - \lambda I)\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}$ has a nonzero solution $\iff$ $A - \lambda I$ is singular:
the **characteristic equation**. Then solve $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}$ for each root.

Check: trace $4 = 3 + 1$; determinant $3 = 3\times1$. The eigenvectors are orthogonal, as they always are for a symmetric matrix with distinct eigenvalues (for a repeated eigenvalue they can be chosen orthogonal).

| Property | Statement |
| --- | --- |
| Trace | $\sum\lambda_i = \mathrm{tr}(A)$ ([Trace of a Matrix](note:trace-of-a-matrix)) |
| Determinant | $\prod\lambda_i = \det(A)$ — so singular iff some $\lambda = 0$ |
| Powers / inverse | $A^k$ has eigenvalues $\lambda^k$; $A^{-1}$ has $1/\lambda$ |
| Symmetric $A$ | All eigenvalues real; eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues orthogonal, and an orthogonal set can always be chosen ([Spectral Decomposition](note:spectral-decomposition)) |
| Idempotent $A$ | $\lambda \in \{0, 1\}$, since $\lambda^2 = \lambda$ |

- **Econometrics**: the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{M}$ are 0s and 1s, so trace = rank ([Projection Matrix and Residual Maker](note:projection-matrix-and-residual-maker)); definiteness of $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}$ ([Quadratic Forms and Definiteness](note:quadratic-forms-and-definiteness)); near-zero eigenvalues of $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}$ signal multicollinearity.
- **Time series / dynamics**: a system $\mathbf{x}_t = A\mathbf{x}_{t-1}$ is stable iff all $|\lambda| < 1$ ([Geometric Series](note:geometric-series)).
